project.name: eslint-plugin-anti-slop
project.identity: An ESLint plugin that catches low-signal AI and code-review patterns before they land in JavaScript and TypeScript code.
project.audience: JavaScript and TypeScript teams that want focused signal-quality checks in local lint and CI workflows.
project.core_loop: Run lint rules against a code change, report low-signal patterns with actionable locations, fix or consciously review them, and use the same checks in CI.
project.north_star: Low-signal generated or review-shaped code is made visible early enough for a team to improve it before it becomes shared code.
not_this: A universal style or correctness judge
A model client or autonomous refactoring service
A license to reject code without explainable rule evidence

mvp.definition: The package installs and exposes focused anti-slop rules that produce actionable ESLint diagnostics for supported JavaScript and TypeScript patterns.

complete_product.definition: The plugin provides a stable, explainable rule set with low false-positive risk, documented configuration, and reliable local and CI adoption across supported codebases.

outcomes.name: Teams receive focused diagnostics that identify low-signal patterns and support a human fix or review decision.

layers.intended: The plugin improves code signal without pretending to replace engineering judgment.
layers.planned: The package exposes rules and configuration for anti-slop patterns.
layers.implemented: An active ESLint package contains the rule implementation and package surface.
layers.verified: RuleTester coverage plus linked and packed consumer smokes exercise representative JavaScript/JSX and TypeScript/TSX parser paths without parser or configuration failures; expected placeholder findings remain observable.
